synthesis: ClickhouseHttpClient::request() throws ClickhouseException with a parsed message and nothing else. The SQL is a local in select()/write(). ClickhouseException does not extend Illuminate QueryException, so HasRetryQuery's SQL log never runs for it. Org cache warms, hit metric cards, and ClickhouseQuery::query() each swallow or re-report the thin message. A platform subclass of the HTTP client, installed by re-extending the clickhouse driver from a booted() callback, can log truncated SQL and the App caller on db-error and rethrow the original exception. That covers select, statement, and insert without a laravel-clickhouse change. query_id is not on the exception; the ticket treats it as optional.

recommendation.escalate_if: A later phase makes ClickHouse query_id mandatory. Capturing X-ClickHouse-Query-Id means editing private request() in insight-lpr/laravel-clickhouse. That is outside this prep and needs an explicit escalate before Implement.
recommendation.why_not_package: Public select() and write() still have the SQL and the bindings when request() throws. The platform already replaces the connection client in tests. Subclassing the client and re-registering the driver records every HTTP failure that uses the app connection, then rethrows so current catches keep working.
recommendation.why_not_exception_handler_only: Org.php, HasRetryQuery, HasHitMetricCards, and ClickhouseQuery::query() swallow ClickhouseException before or instead of a useful db-error line. bootstrap/app.php only special-cases PostgreSQL 57014. A report() hook misses the swallowed paths.
proposed_shape: Add a platform subclass of LaravelClickhouseEloquent\ClickhouseHttpClient. Override select() and write() only. insert() calls $this->write(), so one write() override covers inserts.
On ClickhouseException, log one db-error record and rethrow the same instance. Do not wrap it and do not change its message. getCode() stays 0; parse ch_code from the message.

Add a platform subclass of LaravelClickhouseEloquent\Connection that overrides createWithClient() and assigns the logging client. Parent::createWithClient() uses new static and then overwrites client with the stock client, so the override is required.

Register the clickhouse driver again inside AppServiceProvider's booted() callback. ClickhouseServiceProvider is listed after AppServiceProvider in bootstrap/providers.php, so a boot() extend() would lose.

Leave timeout_query, timeout_connect, retries, settings, LprRepossessions, and HeldFlexibleCache unchanged. Read the numbers off the config array passed into the client constructor and copy them into the log.
Do not log on the success path.

fields.sql: The SQL argument, truncated. Use the key sql so extract_sql_queries.py sees it. For select, this is the statement before the client appends ' FORMAT JSON'.

candidates.note: Names short list queries. Likely to clip company-metrics SQL before the WHERE.
Recommended. Head-biased. Large enough for a typical dashboard statement, small enough that a polygon literal cannot fill the log file. Record sql_original_length either way.
Use only if Plan measures a real product statement whose identifying WHERE starts after 4096 characters.

truncation_candidates.style: Keep the head. Suffix with '…[truncated N chars]' when cut. Do not log head and tail unless 4096 clips the identifying predicate; that choice is Plan's.

bindings.overflow: drop the tail and set bindings_truncated true

sql_and_bindings: Replace case-insensitive password, secret, token, api_key, api-key, and authorization assignments (key=value or key: value) with [redacted].
Do not interpolate bindings into the logged SQL. Log the placeholder statement plus bindings_redacted so a secret can be masked before it is written.
Do not redact plates, org ids, or other query predicates. The point of the line is to name the query.

whereRaw literals are already inside the SQL argument (the CH driver inlines some array literals). They are covered by truncation and the credential regex, not by a second pass that strips every string.
redaction_rules.preexisting_pii: DataDogHandler still adds user name and email on this channel. Out of scope to remove. New fields use ids only.
redaction_rules.successful_queries: No log line. No extra query. No settings write. A timer around the parent call is the only added work, and only the failure path writes.
